refusals.head: core_promise_weakened
refusals.where: definition.md, runner-up paragraph; owner_pages.md, Signature line; ambiguities.md (no row for these words)
refusals.evidence: The owner's typed experience row (design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md:27) is: "Sticky, stinking, slow to move or burn or surrender. The sump hides all and makes you fight it for every action." The proposal says the signature was chosen "from your experience sentence" and that the sentence "concerns ordinary resistance". It uses only "fight it for every action" and "slow to move". It never settles "hides all", "slow to burn", "slow to surrender" or "stinking". "Hides all" is the half of his sentence that supports the runner-up: the archive, and "everything that ever blundered in is still in there" (the_sump.md §1). It also pulls against B1, whose whole promise is that the settler CAN tell deep, shallow and solid apart. Tar fire is kept as ordinary FlowWorks fire, with no argument about "slow to burn".
refusals.would_pass: An ambiguity row for each of these phrases gives two readings, the reading taken and the evidence. Either "hides all" is shown to be met in 0.1.0 (for example, figuratively, by a deep-versus-shallow danger that inspection reveals but a glance does not), or it is named on his pages as consciously deferred along with excavation. The runner-up paragraph stops saying his sentence is only about resistance.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add one ambiguities.md row covering "hides all / slow to burn / slow to surrender / stinking". Change the owner_pages Signature line so it states that "hides all" moves to the next version with the archive, or that B1 keeps it in a stated form.

refusals.head: kept_mechanic_undefined
refusals.where: bars.json B7 range and start; B3 accept picture 3; census.json native-hydration row (line ~1019); definition.md Neighbours
refusals.evidence: B7 requires "human drinking-water provision, water hauling and thirst searches at default FlowWorks settings" over at least 60 days. Its start says only: "Supply ordinary colonist drinking water through existing provisions/engines; natural tar is not fresh water for humanlikes." The census row says "colonists retain ordinary supplied drinking-water needs". The frozen sheet bans rain and surface water (the_sump.md §6 ban 4: "No rain, no surface water defs — the only liquid is tar"), and the BiomeDef records "no precipitation at all". FlowWorks thirst applies to pawns who drink terrain (modledger FlowWorks.json:779). Nothing names where a colonist's water comes from for a season. So the whole bar either rests on a source that is never defined, or on starting stock that runs out (a stall that looks like the signature failing).
refusals.would_pass: A named, existing, ban-compliant water source for humanlikes and tame non-native animals on the Sump, or an explicit statement that human thirst is out of scope at shipped defaults with its source, plus a census row and a ticket if the source is unbuilt. B7's reject list includes "colony dehydrates for lack of any legal water source".
refusals.smallest_fix: Add one census row and one rule naming the colonist water supply, with a ticket if it is absent. Put it in B7's start in place of "existing provisions/engines".

refusals.head: figurative_unmarked
refusals.where: bars.json B1 'says' ("flat black basin"); B7 'says' ("living margins", "dusky black ground")
refusals.evidence: ambiguities.md settles "Flat" as non-literal: "Flat skyline and continuous low ground; shoreline geometry can be irregular". It settles "Black basin" as "Black pools and glass sheets dominate the player's terrain reading", not as all ground being black, since margins carry grey-green plants. Yet B1 and B7 both have "figurative": [] and no accept picture that departs from the literal reading. B6 also uses "burden" unmarked, though B4 marks it.
refusals.would_pass: Each of these words is listed in that bar's figurative list with what it stands for and one accept picture that departs from the literal reading (an irregular shoreline, vegetated margins on non-black ground).
refusals.smallest_fix: Copy the two ambiguity readings into the figurative lists of B1 and B7, each with one departing accept picture. Add the B4 "burden" entry to B6.

stranger.text: Lamp-lit work areas remain recognizably part of the dark basin; no native plant supplies the light.
Fog and black shading make a safe solid approach indistinguishable from deep tar, or the sky cycles into rain or daylight.
The horizon stays low and amber, black pools differ from solid sheets and their shallow margins, and a settler can choose a connected solid patch for stores and shelter.
A grass meadow tinted dark has an isolated tar ornament, while most work and walking ignore the basin.
Skelver and lanneth can be gathered on eligible margins, a sown dorvel bed advances in dusk without a lamp, and temperature inspection explains a colder bed that has stopped.
Margin plants fill distant dry ground, or a harmless default plant tells the player it identifies gas, treasure or a collapsing floor.
Edible plants resolve in the database but a forager cannot harvest food, or dorvel only advances under a sunlamp.
Pale crust and pool film occupy their declared solid or tar habitats without claiming to reveal a buried trap.
Mice feed and cross their shallow-tar habitat while skarrid hunt, a permitted tame attempt proceeds by ordinary work, and a skellarn flight state carries it across a ground barrier.
A native dehydrates beside accessible home tar because the shared native-water binding is absent.
A native animal meets its thirst at the tar margin without human liquid penalties; settlers use their ordinary supplied drinking water.
A plain kethrel eats and can be managed without stealing scrap; an animal that dies leaves a corpse or a readable ordinary exit.
A skellarn has a flight stat but never enters flight, or a mouse is as mired as a colonist despite its adapted movement fiction.
Animals spawn for the photograph but cannot reach suitable food or complete a normal hunt/tame job in their habitat.
A worker reaches clean ground and instantly forgets all exposure, or quietly disappears into tar instead of retaining a readable recoverable state.
The floor looks dirty but neither the carrier nor subsequent work pays a cost, or a health penalty appears without any actual shallow-tar pickup.
An outdoor worker takes a shallow shortcut, returns tarred, leaves tar on an accepting floor and performs the same ordinary work more slowly than when clean.
A worker avoiding tar stays unexposed while the dirty worker retains readable state after reaching solid ground and reloading.
A dirty carrier crosses glasswalk without laying new tar there, then uses a real accepting cleanup location rather than becoming magically clean.
Regular traffic leaves the glasswalk clear while a nearby ordinary accepting floor fouls; the same clean walking worker still takes longer on glasswalk than on clean paving.
Glasswalk is a perfectly fast paved highway, or its label promises a clean route while tar deposits remain on it.
The apparent route advantage exists only because the comparison lane was dark or the worker had different gear, and the terrain itself supplies no tradeoff.
A cure teleports solvent from a sealed room, consumes it twice after interruption, causes a medical injury or endlessly retries instead of doing ordinary work.
When solvent is missing or unreachable, the action names the shortage and yields to ordinary work or slower clean-ground recovery without demanding repeated player clicks.
After outside work, an available worker uses accessible reserved solvent under the colony policy, returns to ordinary work and stays recovered until newly exposed.
The player must place a new medical bill on each dirty worker after each trip, or the bill removes only the condition and dirty boots immediately give it back.

Across settlement and continued outside work, paths improve and solvent stock is spent and replenished, plants are harvested and regrow where eligible, animals feed, and dirty areas remain without halting meals, hauling and construction after a reload.
Raw tar or uncontrolled plant spread consumes the usable settlement, or the map becomes empty of ordinary native life despite suitable food and temperature.
Workers repeatedly reserve cleanup forever while food and ordinary work stop, or reload duplicates stock, loses pawns, activates deferred systems or produces a repeating error storm.

Building routes before rendering solvent or rendering solvent before extending routes produces different inconvenience but neither order needs a debug cure, a hidden extra or a locked sky to keep the colony working.

rounds.missed_capability: The census has no row for the water supply of colonists and tame non-native animals on a biome where the frozen sheet bans rain and surface water and tar is not potable. The native-hydration row only asserts "colonists retain ordinary supplied drinking-water needs" and names no supply, yet B7's season run turns FlowWorks thirst on at defaults.
rounds.loop_or_three_way: The solvent chain loops back on itself. Weak solvent comes only from butchered thrummel/broodmother seepwax (R9; RM_Tarred_Solvents.xml costList RM_Seepwax). Hunting those animals sends hunters across shallow-tar margins, which tars them (B4). Tarred hunters create more solvent demand (B6), which needs more hunting (R9), while B3 and B7 require the wildlife to persist and stay huntable. The 'animals', 'cleanup' and 'carried' meetings each hold one edge of this loop, but no meeting argues the cycle B3→B4→B6→R9→B3 as one group or names the Solvent queue plus Whole map run that would show whether it drains the food web.

refusals.head: kept_mechanic_undefined
refusals.where: definition.md §Using it / §What changes in the colony's story; bars.json B6; tickets.md T40; census.json row routine_cleaning
refusals.evidence: routine_cleaning is built: absent, fate needed_by signature, and B6 depends on it. It is defined only as "the player's standing cleaning/work priorities and solvent-reserve policy" (definition.md) and "an enable/reserve policy" (T40). Several things are left open. Which work type does the job. What triggers it: carried tar, or a given RM_Tarred stage. Whether the tarred pawn cleans itself or "an available helper/pawn" does it. Where it happens: definition.md says "a stocked cleanup station matter[s]", but no census row, ticket or building is a station. What the "reserve policy" actually is: a Mod Setting, a stockpile or a per-pawn toggle. The source answer this cites (design/RimMandrake/designer_codex_2026-11-09/TheSump/ANSWERS_OWNER.md: "workers clean ... on their own; he plans routes ... and spends scarce solvent") splits what workers do unprompted from what he spends, and the proposal never says on which side automatic solvent use falls. Two builders would make two different mods: a self-queued scrub surgery, or a new WorkGiver at a station.
refusals.would_pass: One paragraph that fixes the routine's work type, trigger, actor (self or helper), place (any clean accepting cell, or a named building) and the player control that decides when scarce solvent is spent as opposed to ordinary unprompted cleaning, mirrored in T40's specification and acceptance test.
refusals.smallest_fix: Add that paragraph to definition.md §Using it and to T40. Delete "stocked cleanup station" unless a building is commissioned, and state which side of his ANSWERS_OWNER split automatic solvent use sits on.

refusals.head: core_promise_weakened
refusals.where: bars.json B3 says and range; definition.md §When it goes wrong ("Natural deep tar is impassable to ordinary ground walkers")
refusals.evidence: The owner-starred mouse promise is "run easily over the tar without a thought" (the_sump.md §4), "Mice run the black" (§5), and "Mice run the tar without a thought. Nothing else touches it" (§1, repeated in the RM_TheSump BiomeDef description). B3 narrows this to "mice cross shallow tar without colonist mire". Its range lists only "mouse shallow crossings", while the definition makes deep tar impassable and gives mice no exception. Census native_tar_crossing even names a "tar-cost/entry exemption", entry being what deep tar needs. Deferring the mouse-line instrument (T23) does not require shrinking where mice run.
refusals.would_pass: B3 and its range cover mice crossing the tar, deep pools included, at their ordinary pace while colonists cannot. Or a marked, delegated argument for excluding deep tar, with the biome description corrected so it does not promise more.
refusals.smallest_fix: Change B3's "shallow tar" to "the tar, shallow and deep", add deep-pool mouse crossings to B3's range and T44's acceptance test, and add a mouse exception to the definition's deep-tar sentence.

refusals.head: contradicts_ruling_or_lore
refusals.where: census.json row dusk_weather (fate land); bars.json R10; ambiguities.md row "Permanent dusk" ("No special sun value")
refusals.evidence: The kept land row includes a "biome glow multiplier and sunlight-stat suppression". The BiomeDef sets BiomeGlowMultiplierExtension glowMultiplier 0.55 and suppressSunlightStatAffecter true (RM_TheSump_Biome.xml:175-177). EnvironmentalHazards' BiomeGlowMultiplierExtension.cs describes the flag as making a biome "permanently sunless rather than merely dim". That is a per-biome sun override. Standing ruling, 2026-10-19 card (standing_rulings.md:156): "no biome-specific heat, no biome-specific sun. It's a matter of geometry". The proposal also says "No special sun value" and "under the fixed world's geometry" while keeping both biome-specific sun fields unexamined. The site's sun is already −10.6° below the horizon (the_sump.md §0), so geometry alone may give the dusk.
refusals.would_pass: Either the dusk is defined as coming from the fixed site's geometric sun angle, with the glow multiplier and sunlight suppression moved out of land; or a written argument that a light-only multiplier is not a "sun" under that ruling, with the suppress flag's effect named and shown to touch no Direct Sun or heat path.
refusals.smallest_fix: Name both fields in dusk_weather and R10 and decide each: drop them, or argue them past the Direct Sun ruling. Remove "No special sun value" if they stay.

refusals.head: check_or_rule_as_bar
refusals.where: bars.json B7 accept picture "Settlers drink carried fresh water ... the declared expedition stock lasts through the run ..."; B3 accept picture "... settlers drink carried fresh-water bottles or draw from imported fresh-water barrels"
refusals.evidence: "The declared expedition stock lasts through the run" holds by construction: T51 and B7's range tell the tester to budget cargo for "the complete 60-day-or-longer declared horizon ... contingency reserve" and to "Extend the finite budget if the run extends". That is R12, our provisioning rule, and C10's debit reconciliation. It is a test-setup condition, not something the player experiences, and it cannot fail because of the mod. B3 is an animal bar, and its says names no humanlike drinking, yet its accept picture puts settler bottle drinking in as a pass condition.
refusals.would_pass: Water provisioning sits in R12, B7's sees.start and C10. B7's picture keeps only what the player sees: settlers drink carried water with thirst on and no pond, while natives drink at the tar. B3's pictures are about animals only, with the humanlike case kept as a sees.control.
refusals.smallest_fix: Cut "the declared expedition stock lasts through the run" from B7's accept picture. Cut the settler clause from B3's accept picture and move it to B3's sees.control.

refusals.head: figurative_unmarked
refusals.where: bars.json B4 says ("carries tar home"); B6 says ("standing work orders")
refusals.evidence: "home" in B4 is not literal: the accept picture means any accepting floor, not RimWorld's Home area or the base. "standing work orders" in B6 is not a RimWorld object: vanilla has work priorities and bills, and a reader could take a single repeating bill as a standing order. Neither word is in its bar's figurative list. B4 lists only "burden", B6 lists only "burden".
refusals.would_pass: Each word is either listed as figurative, with what it stands for and an accept picture that departs from the literal reading, or replaced with literal words.
refusals.smallest_fix: In B4 write "carries tar onto accepting floors". In B6 write "following work priorities and the colony's solvent setting", or add both words to the figurative lists with stands_for and accept pictures.

rounds.missed_capability: Floor fouling and its removal. RM_Filth_Tar tracked onto ordinary accepting floors carries its own path cost: the RM_SumpWalkways.xml header says "RM_Filth_Tar, pathCost 34 ... is what actually slows a fouled duckboard cell". Vanilla Cleaning work then removes it from floors. No census row covers the filth def, the slowdown on fouled floors, or the floor-cleaning labour, even though definition.md relies on them ("Dirt remains on ordinary floors", "A clean glasswalk approach needs no floor scrubbing"). This is the other half of glasswalk's tradeoff. B5 compares glasswalk only with clean paving and never with fouled paving, which is the case that makes a permanently slower floor worth laying. The Solvent queue model also leaves floor-cleaning labour out of its competing-labour inputs.
rounds.loop_or_three_way: Tar fire, margin plants and the absence of rain form a loop the meetings split apart. R2 puts natural margin plants on dry cells 1 to 3 cells from tar. B7 requires lit natural tar to keep burning (its accept picture: "remains an ongoing visible fire hazard"), and FlowWorks RM_LiquidFire.cs agrees: "a limitless source burns forever". On the Sump only firefoam or rain puts a burning cell out, and the dusk lock rules out rain ("it does not rain"). B7 also requires "living margins" that "regrow where eligible". The growth meeting (B2, B3, B7, R2, R6, R7, R9, R10) leaves out R11 and fire, and the liquid meeting (B1, B5, B7, R6, R11, R12) leaves out R2 and B2. If a burning tar cell lights or heats the plants next to it (unread; I did not check whether it does), one ignition of a connected mere becomes a lasting ring of fire that re-burns every regrowing margin plant. B2 and B7's margin picture would then fail, even though each pair of bars and rules holds on its own. This belongs in the Whole map model as a named branch: ignition beside the margins, with the fire source's reach and its effect on adjacent plants read.
